text:
emily (AE): FYI — Prospect (CedarLine) pushing DPA redlines that demand KMS attestation + access to key metadata before we flip them to production. They also flagged DocuSign as outbound-blocked. Procurement wants Net60 on the PO. Need a fast path so Dedicated POC isn't delayed.

Ravi (Infra): Short answer: we can produce a tenant-scoped KMS/HSM attestation signed by our HSM in ~3 business days if scope is limited to the keys used for their tenant. We can't export keys or provide full key material. If they insist on metadata access, legal needs to narrow "metadata" to non-sensitive fields.

Kai (Legal): Paste the exact redline if you have it. High level: we can add a 1-page addendum: "Vendor will provide a signed attestation limited to cryptographic material used by Customer within 7 business days of request. Vendor will not disclose private key material. Onsite or on-prem validation requires separate SOW."

emily (AE): Redline snippet: "Vendor must provide KMS attestation and allow Customer audit access to key metadata and usage logs prior to production onboarding."

Kai (Legal): Proposed edit to counter: `Vendor will provide a signed attestation covering key identifiers and usage patterns relevant to Customer's tenant; Vendor will not disclose private keying material or internal KMS operator logs. Audit access limited to tenant-scoped usage summaries and delivered via secure report.` I'll draft and attach.

Nora (Finance): Net60 increases exposure. For POCs under $25k we default to Net30. If CedarLine insists on Net60, we need CFO signoff plus either a $20k refundable hold or milestone-based billing (50% upfront). Also invoice must include PO number and remit instructions.

emily (AE): They estimated the POC at ~$22k. I'll ask procurement if Net60 is mandatory.

Ravi (Infra): On signatures: since DocuSign egress is blocked, options are: (A) they whitelist our signing IP 3.24.18.0/24 for a short window, (B) they upload signed PDFs to our secure portal (we store hash+audit), (C) we use a browser-based hosted signing flow that doesn't require outbound egress from their network (works if their browser policy allows). Option C often satisfies SecOps because signing happens client-side and only the signed artifact is uploaded.

signing-bot: Uploaded contract redline: https://secure.docs/redwood/cedarline/msa_dpa_redline_v1.pdf — checklist: [KMS addendum] [Net terms decision] [Signature fallback confirmed] [SOC2 link sent]

Kai (Legal): I'll draft the KMS addendum with explicit scope and the portal-upload signature clause: `Signed PDF uploaded to Vendor secure portal with hash recorded in Vendor audit logs and mirrored email confirmation shall be deemed a valid signature.` Will also enumerate allowed metadata fields.

Nora (Finance): If PO stays ~22k => Net30 acceptable. If they push Net60, route to me and I'll start the CFO approval + hold conversation.

emily (AE): Action items: 1) I'll confirm whether Net60 is mandatory, 2) ask SecOps if they can whitelist signing IP or accept portal/upload/hosted-browser option, 3) attach procurement PO when ready. Kai: drop the addendum and I'll send it to them.

Ravi (Infra): FYI provisioning timeline: once contracts are countersigned and tenant attestation requested, Dedicated POC provisioning ~10 business days. If they require on-prem validation or extended audits, add 6-8 weeks.

emily (AE): Thanks all — I'll update here as soon as procurement replies. :pray:
